ambush.name: Ambush strike
ambush.reading: strikes before the other can act: a sit-and-wait or burst hunter

pursuit.name: Pursuit
pursuit.reading: runs down what flees: a chaser

theft.name: Theft
theft.reading: takes what others hold: a kleptoparasite of other foragers

sedative.name: Sedative
sedative.reading: puts others to sleep: a forager that disarms its food or its threats

lithic.name: Rock and soil
lithic.reading: rock, sand and soil: a digging or cliff lineage

flora.name: Plants
flora.reading: a plant-associated lineage: seeds, roots, spores

aerial.name: Flight
aerial.reading: an aerial lineage: wind and height

shadow.name: Darkness
shadow.reading: a nocturnal lineage: works in the dark

social.name: Cooperation
social.reading: lives with others: care, calls and help

recovery.name: Recovery
recovery.reading: heals and outlasts: a lineage of hard places

armour.name: Armour
armour.reading: defended or retaliatory: takes the hit, or returns it

display.name: Power display
display.reading: builds itself up before it commits: display, dominance, a dance

mind.name: Mind
mind.reading: a psychic lineage: foresight and the mind

cur.name: Rooted meadow-sitter
cur.reading: Ingrain puts down roots that feed the user but stop it fleeing, Curse trades speed for toughness, and Amnesia steadies its resistance. Together they describe a lineage that stops following the sun and roots instead, the reverse of 3.1's 'stays on the move'. Fits rich, reliably sunny meadows where staying put pays.
cur.behavior: Settles into one sunny patch for weeks and won't be moved.

cur.name: Lullaby bloom
cur.reading: Grass Whistle is a soothing melody that puts the listener to sleep, Charm softens an attacker, and Safeguard protects against status harm. A lineage that pacifies rather than fights, extending the calming aroma of 3.8 to sound. Fits meadows shared with many large grazers, or a homestead.
cur.behavior: Hums and wafts scent until the quarrel around it stops.

cur.name: Shade bramble
cur.reading: Sludge is a poisonous splash and Power Whip a heavy lash of vines. A lineage that spends less on basking and more on defence, poisoning and whipping what comes close. Fits damp, part-shaded woodland edges where sunlight is short and the plant on its back can't carry it alone.
cur.behavior: Sits low in the undergrowth and lashes out with vines.

cur.name: Crag duellist
cur.reading: Dragon Dance raises speed and strength, read here as a display before a fight; Dragon Rush is a full-body charge and Outrage a sustained rampage. A lineage that settles contests with rivals by display and then open combat, the adult's search for strong opponents made central. Fits high crags where flying rivals meet.
cur.behavior: Displays from a high perch, then dives at the challenger.

cur.name: Scree hunter
cur.reading: Rock Slide and Ancient Power bring stone down or hurl it, and Metal Claw is a hard-edged slash. A lineage that works broken rock, loosening scree onto whatever is below and finishing with claws. Fits steep, rocky mountains like those where Charmeleon live.
cur.behavior: Hunts along cliff edges, sending stones down before it follows.

cur.name: Pack raider
cur.reading: Beat Up is an attack the user's companions all join, and Bite and Crunch are jaw attacks. A lineage that hunts or fights in groups and uses its jaws more than its fire. Fits mountain valleys where many Charmeleon live within sight of one another.
cur.behavior: Attacks as a group; the jaws do the work, the fire is held back.

cur.name: Silt-pond stalker
cur.reading: Mud Sport and Muddy Water both cloud things with mud, and Foresight picks out what is hidden. A lineage of murky, still water that hides in its own silt and still finds its prey, the Wartortle habit of stalking from hiding taken further. Fits shallow, muddy ponds and marsh pools.
cur.behavior: Stirs up the bottom, waits in the cloud, and strikes at what it can see but its prey can't.

cur.name: Mist-lake elder
cur.reading: Mist shrouds the user in fog, Aqua Ring wraps it in a veil of water that slowly heals, and Refresh clears poison, burns and paralysis. A lineage built for slow recovery and long life rather than fighting, which suits a line famous for longevity. Fits cold, misty highland lakes where individuals live long enough to grow algae on their shells.
cur.behavior: Slow, rarely seen, and very old; heals rather than fights.

cur.name: Jet charger
cur.reading: Aqua Jet is a lunge so fast it is almost invisible, Water Spout is strongest when the user is unhurt, and Fake Out is a surprise opening blow. A lineage that opens every encounter with an overwhelming burst, the 'jets used for high-speed tackles' of 9.1 made central. Fits open, fast rivers where a fight is won in the first moment.
cur.behavior: Hits first and hardest, then withdraws into its shell.

cur.name: Storm capacitor
cur.reading: A store-and-release lineage: Charge builds up power for the next electric move, Bide absorbs punishment and returns it doubled, and Reversal hits hardest when it is nearly beaten. It is the cheek-pouch canon (pent-up energy released in one burst) made into a fighting style. Fits exposed ridges and hilltops with frequent thunderstorms, where charge comes easily.
cur.behavior: Holds back, soaks up, then releases everything at once.

cur.name: Kin keeper
cur.reading: A caring lineage built on the Platinum canon of recharging a weakened companion: Wish heals whoever is in its place next turn, Present can heal or harm, and Encore holds an attacker to one move while others act. Fits dense forest groups where weak members are kept going rather than left.
cur.behavior: Stays close to injured groupmates; tends rather than flees.

cur.name: Spark-sparrer
cur.reading: Play-fighting kept into adulthood: Fake Out startles, Double Slap is a contact contest of quick light blows, and Tickle weakens without injuring. Low-harm moves that settle disputes, like Pichu's tail-touching tests of courage. Fits large, crowded groups where real fights would be costly.
cur.behavior: Settles rank with sparring rather than shocks.

cur.name: Sleep-feeder
cur.reading: A lineage of stealthy blood-feeders that put a host to sleep and approach unseen. Fits places with large animals that sleep in the open or in roosts: pastures, bird roosts, people's houses.
cur.behavior: Feeds on sleeping hosts and leaves before they wake.
cur.analogy: Common vampire bats (Desmodus rotundus) feed mostly on sleeping livestock at night.

cur.name: Air hawk
cur.reading: A lineage of fast aerial pursuers catching flying prey on the wing. Fits open forest edges, rivers and lakeshores with swarms of insects at dusk.
cur.behavior: Hunts in open air rather than in the forest interior.

cur.name: Roost guard
cur.reading: A lineage that clears intruders from crowded roosts with wing-driven wind. Fits large colonies in caves or buildings where roost space is contested.
cur.behavior: Drives off intruders and rivals from its roost.

cur.name: Sleep-feeder
cur.reading: A lineage that puts its victim to sleep and approaches unseen, a refinement of striking from behind. Fits caves full of resting animals, like the Ice Path with its Swinub and Jynx.
cur.behavior: Feeds on sleepers; rarely has to fight.
cur.analogy: Common vampire bats feed mostly on sleeping animals at night.

cur.name: Open-air pursuer
cur.reading: Moves that hit a fleeing target, strike first and dive hard: a chasing lineage for the open night sky over Route 45 and the cave mouths rather than tight passages.
cur.behavior: Hunts outside; returns to roost before dawn.

cur.name: Roost holder
cur.reading: Wind moves that blow rivals away: a lineage that defends roost space in crowded colonies. Fits the high-ceilinged chambers of the Ice Path, where Zubat and Golbat roost together.
cur.behavior: Drives others off the best ceiling spots.

cur.name: Rooted settler
cur.reading: A lineage that leans further into the plant side of its life: it roots in harder and longer (Ingrain) and draws energy from light (Synthesis) instead of wandering. Fits stable, fertile clearings where staying put pays better than seeding new ground.
cur.behavior: Wanders less and stays planted for days, leaves held up to the light.

cur.name: Blade-leaf
cur.reading: A lineage that arms its leaves: sharp-edged leaves thrown or slashed at attackers. Fits grassland and forest edges with more grazers or predators, where the leaves a buried Oddish leaves showing (43.8) are what gets bitten.
cur.behavior: Fights back with its leaves instead of shrieking and staying put.

cur.name: Distraction dancer
cur.reading: A lineage that defuses attackers with behaviour rather than chemistry: a confusing dance, a disarming display, tickling. Fits places with many casual predators, and it foreshadows the line's later dancing (Bellossom).
cur.behavior: Dances and fusses when cornered.

cur.name: Lure-and-bite
cur.reading: A lineage that adds animal food to root sap: a scent lure to bring small animals close, a bite, and a strike at whatever turns to flee. Fits poor soils where roots yield little.
cur.behavior: Sits scented at a burrow mouth and snaps at visitors.

cur.name: Stone-claw digger
cur.reading: A lineage built for hard ground: hardened claws for burrowing through stony or root-bound soil, and Counter for whatever digs it up. Fits rocky ground and caves such as Mt. Moon, where Paras also lives.
cur.behavior: Digs deeper and hits back when unearthed.

cur.name: Bug-led
cur.reading: A lineage in which the bug keeps the upper hand for longer: fast, with venomous claws, able to forage beyond the dark, damp places the mushroom prefers (47.3). Fits drier, more open woodland.
cur.behavior: Moves about more by day and burrows less.

cur.name: Mind-mushroom
cur.reading: The tochukaso already gives the host orders (46.5) and seems to do the thinking in Parasect (47.2); a psychic attack in the lineage reads as that control turned outward, against attackers. Fits crowded infestations where many Paras share one tree.
cur.behavior: Unsettles attackers instead of fleeing them.

cur.name: Seer
cur.reading: A lineage in which the power is stronger and steadier, with a flavour of anticipation (Future Sight, Foresight). Fits waters with many threats, where early warning pays.
cur.behavior: Fewer blackouts, more deliberate use of its power.

cur.name: Drowsy lure
cur.reading: A lineage that disarms threats by making them sleepy or confused, turning the 'vacant look' that lulls enemies (54.1) into a real tactic. Fits ponds with many predators and few hiding places.
cur.behavior: Stares, yawns, and lets attackers lose interest.

cur.name: Mud-bank brawler
cur.reading: A physical lineage of muddy pond margins, flinging mud and striking with its arms, using its upright body. Fits shallow, silty ponds and marsh.
cur.behavior: Fights on the bank rather than retreating to open water.

cur.name: Shallows brawler
cur.reading: A lineage that fights hand to hand and flings mud. Fits muddy rivers and marshes where visibility is poor and prey or rivals are met at close range.
cur.behavior: Wades and grapples instead of sprinting.

cur.name: Hypnotic hunter
cur.reading: A lineage that stuns or confuses with its power before the chase, saving the sprint. Fits big lakes where prey is spread out and chases are long.
cur.behavior: Forehead glowing, it stalks before it swims.

cur.name: Sentinel
cur.reading: A watchful lineage: it sees through evasion, strikes later, and shakes off status conditions. Fits rough coasts where its rescues are described (55.7) and danger is frequent.
cur.behavior: Patrols shorelines and comes to trouble rather than avoiding it.

cur.name: Dawn howler
cur.reading: Howl is a rallying cry that raises the user's strength, and Morning Sun restores it in sunlight. A lineage of open country that howls across a large territory at first light and recovers by basking. Fits wide, sunny prairies like the one on the ancient scroll.
cur.behavior: Howls from a rise at dawn, then lies out in the early sun.

cur.name: Grassfire driver
cur.reading: Fire Spin traps a target in a ring of flame, Heat Wave sweeps a wide area, and Flare Blitz is a burning charge. A lineage that uses fire to herd and corner rather than just to strike. Fits dry grassland, and is the most dangerous to keep near people and crops.
cur.behavior: Rings its quarry with fire, then charges.

cur.name: Flock guardian
cur.reading: Safeguard shields companions from status harm, Crunch is a crushing bite, and Body Slam pins with weight. A lineage that guards a group, holding intruders off with bite and bulk. Fits upland pasture with herds or flocks to protect, close to Growlithe's loyalty to its trainer.
cur.behavior: Lies among the animals it guards and gets up only for intruders.

cur.name: Cold-water
cur.reading: Three Ice-type egg moves: a lineage at home in cold, high water. Fits highland ponds and streams like Blackthorn City's and Route 44's, where Poliwag is in fact found.
cur.behavior: Stays active in cold water and under thin ice.

cur.name: Mud-bottom
cur.reading: A lineage of silty, shallow ponds: mud as weapon and cover, and resistance to the infections and fouling of stagnant water (Refresh cures status problems).
cur.behavior: Lives on and in the muddy bottom.

cur.name: Splash-escape
cur.reading: A lineage that leaps clear of the water to escape, and fights hardest when badly hurt. Fits ponds with many fast predators, where a last-ditch escape matters.
cur.behavior: Jumps when chased; turns on an attacker when cornered.

cur.name: Elemental fist
cur.reading: Three punches that each carry an element. A lineage that does fight hand to hand, making up for weak muscles with fire, cold and charge delivered on contact. It runs against the adult's dislike of physical attacks (65.9). Fits close quarters, such as caves like Granite Cave where foes come within reach before they can be sensed.
cur.behavior: Lets a foe close in, then strikes once, hard, with whatever element suits.

cur.name: Walled sleeper
cur.reading: Barrier raises a sharp defensive wall and Guard Swap trades defensive advantages with a foe. A lineage that protects its long sleep with walls instead of teleporting away. Fits narrow caves and crowded towns where teleporting at random is risky.
cur.behavior: Sleeps behind a barrier and doesn't flee.

cur.name: Trickster
cur.reading: Encore locks a foe into repeating its last move, Knock Off strips what it holds, and Power Trick swaps the user's own attack and defence. A calculating lineage that disarms and controls foes instead of overpowering them, the 'calculates many things' of 65.5 put to work. Fits towns, where people and their objects are always within reach.
cur.behavior: Makes its opponent predictable, then takes its things.

cur.name: Quarry lifter
cur.reading: Rock Slide brings stone down, and Power Trick swaps the user's attack and defence, turning a body hardened by lifting into a weapon. A lineage built around working rock, the boulder-lifting habit of Machop made into a way of life. Fits rocky caves and quarry-like scree such as Mt. Mortar.
cur.behavior: Moves rock all day, whether or not anything needs moving.

cur.name: Patient counterstriker
cur.reading: Meditate builds strength calmly, Counter returns a physical blow twice as hard, and Light Screen blunts special attacks. A lineage that waits and returns force rather than leaping in first, the opposite of 68.6's 'leaps into action before it thinks'. Fits narrow passes where foes come one at a time.
cur.behavior: Stands still and lets the other animal make the first mistake.

cur.name: Flurry boxer
cur.reading: Bullet Punch is a jab that lands first, Close Combat an all-out exchange that leaves the user open, and Rolling Kick a spinning strike. A lineage built entirely on speed and volume of blows, the thousand punches in two seconds of 68.9. Fits open slopes where fights are short and decided at once.
cur.behavior: Wins in the first second or not at all.

cur.name: Quarry fist
cur.reading: Two heavy arm strikes: a lineage that breaks rock into pieces it can eat or move. Fits bare bedrock and cliff walls with little loose stone, such as the walls of Dark Cave.
cur.behavior: Breaks rock where others graze its surface.

cur.name: Trail sitter
cur.reading: Block stops passage, and Curse (for a non-Ghost) trades speed for strength and toughness. A sedentary lineage that sits half buried on a path and holds its ground; fits busy mountain roads such as Route 45.
cur.behavior: Rarely rolls; stays put and lets the path come to it.

cur.name: Scree runner
cur.reading: Brings rock down and fights hardest when worn down. A lineage of steep, loose slopes and talus below cliffs, where rockfall is the everyday weather.
cur.behavior: Sets off small rockfalls; desperate when cornered.

cur.name: Cliff-cutter
cur.reading: Heavy arm strikes in a lineage that gouges horizontal homes into sheer cliffs (75.10): a burrowing specialist of hard rock faces, such as the cliffs above Route 45.
cur.behavior: Spends more time cutting than rolling; colonies of holes in one face.

cur.name: Avalanche
cur.reading: A lineage that sends rock ahead of itself on the steepest slopes and fights hardest when battered. Fits scree and talus where its rolling sets off rockfalls.
cur.behavior: Rolls in a shower of stones.

cur.name: Roadblock
cur.reading: Block and Curse (slower, stronger, tougher) in a lineage that has given up rolling for holding ground: a Graveler that sits on the trail instead of thundering down it. Fits gentler slopes where rolling gains little.
cur.behavior: Grazes in place; rarely rolls.

cur.name: Marsh lantern
cur.reading: A lineage that lures and startles: Will-O-Wisp is a floating ghost-flame that burns, Astonish is a sudden fright that makes the target flinch. Together they look like the lights that draw travellers off a path. Fits open marsh and moor at night, away from buildings.
cur.behavior: Shows a light, draws the curious close, then frightens them.
cur.analogy: The will-o'-the-wisp of European folklore: lights seen over marshes at night, often attributed to burning marsh gas, though the explanation is still debated.

cur.name: Still-air haze
cur.reading: The gas body as a weapon in sheltered air: Haze spreads a black fog that wipes out every stat change, Disable shuts down an attacker's move, Psywave hits at variable strength. A lineage that fills enclosed spaces rather than drifting outdoors. Fits tower interiors, deep eaves and still caves, where no wind can break it up.
cur.behavior: Stays indoors and fills a room; avoids open ground entirely.

cur.name: Death-song haunt
cur.reading: A lineage that makes itself too costly to kill: Perish Song dooms everything that hears it, Grudge strips the moves of whatever knocks it out, and Explosion takes the attacker with it. Defence by guaranteed retaliation. Fits haunts shared with strong predators, where hiding alone isn't enough.
cur.behavior: Rarely fights; when cornered, ensures the attacker loses too.

cur.name: Silt-bottom
cur.reading: Two mud moves: a lineage of still, muddy water that stirs up silt to hide in or to forage through. Fits cave pools like Dark Cave's, where there is no current to run.
cur.behavior: Stays low; clouds the water when disturbed.

cur.name: Torrent runner
cur.reading: Two powerful water attacks in a lineage built for the fastest water, the strong swimmers that run up falls to spawn. Fits steep highland streams.
cur.behavior: First up the falls in spring.

cur.name: Murk-caster
cur.reading: A psychic beam to disorient and Haze to clear the field: a lineage for murky or lightless water, where disorientation matters more than sight. Fits cave water.
cur.behavior: Defends itself without seeing its attacker.

cur.name: Torrent spawner
cur.reading: Two powerful water attacks in a lineage built for the autumn run up steep, fast streams. Fits highland streams with falls, where the strongest swimmers reach the best nest boulders.
cur.behavior: Nests highest up the stream.

cur.name: Silt nester
cur.reading: Mud moves in a lineage that nests where boulders are scarce, digging into silt and gravel instead of boring rock. Fits slow, muddy reaches and cave pools such as Dark Cave's.
cur.behavior: Digs a hollow rather than drilling one.

cur.name: Heavy guardian
cur.reading: Weight and a tail strike in a nest-guarding lineage that drives intruders off by force. Fits crowded spawning reaches where many pairs nest close together, as when Seaking gather from all over.
cur.behavior: Guards longer and fights harder at the nest.

cur.name: Mirror troupe
cur.reading: Psych Up copies another's state and Wish sends help to whoever is there a moment later: a social lineage that synchronises with and supports others, the move-level echo of making others dance in unison. Fits the larger chambers of the Ice Path, where several could gather.
cur.behavior: Dances in groups; tends the hurt.

cur.name: Clear-eyed
cur.reading: Miracle Eye sees through evasion and Meditate is focus. A perceptive lineage that finds what hides, on top of Forewarn; fits the dark lower floors of the Ice Path.
cur.behavior: Watches more than it dances; the first to notice an intruder.

cur.name: Cold fist
cur.reading: A contact lineage that strikes first and hits with cold fists. Fits passages it shares with Golbat, where it has to defend itself rather than charm.
cur.behavior: Less dance, more fist.

cur.name: Pack-ice breaker
cur.reading: Two one-hit moves that drill and split: Horn Drill with a horn, Fissure by cracking the ground beneath a target. In an Ice-type sea animal they read as tools for breaking ice. A lineage of polar seas, keeping breathing holes and channels open through pack ice.
cur.behavior: Rams and splits ice; travels where others are frozen out.

cur.name: Sleeping voyager
cur.reading: A long-distance lineage: Sleep Talk lets it act while asleep, Refresh clears its own poison, burns and paralysis, and Whirlpool traps a pursuer in a current. An animal that can keep going for days at sea. Fits open ocean crossings far from shore.
cur.behavior: Travels without stopping, resting on the move.
cur.analogy: Dolphins rest one half of the brain at a time (unihemispheric sleep), which lets them keep swimming and surfacing while asleep.

cur.name: Gentle evader
cur.reading: The canon's gentleness as a survival strategy: Substitute leaves a decoy to take the hit, Tickle weakens an attacker without harming it. A lineage that avoids capture and conflict instead of fighting. Fits waters still hunted by people, where the animals that survived are the ones that slipped away.
cur.behavior: Rarely fights; disappears behind a decoy when approached.

cur.name: Last-spark sprinter
cur.reading: Detect sidesteps an attack, Endure survives one that should fell it, and Flail hits harder the closer the user is to defeat. With Jolteon's speed (Quick Attack, Agility), the set describes a lineage that relies on escape first and a desperate counterattack second. Fits open, exposed ground with little cover.
cur.behavior: Runs at the first sign of trouble; cornered, it is at its most dangerous.

cur.name: Mood-charger
cur.reading: Fake Tears and Charm are both emotional displays, one of distress and one of appeal. If every change of mood charges Jolteon, a lineage that displays its feelings often would also stay charged. Fits life in groups, or close to people, where displays get answered.
cur.behavior: Sulks, pleads and sparks in turn; never quite discharged.

cur.name: Pass sleeper
cur.reading: A lineage that cannot be moved: Curse makes it slower, stronger and tougher, and Counter returns physical blows double. The sleeping-roadblock habit as a whole strategy. Fits narrow mountain passes, its listed habitat, where lying across the way keeps a feeding area to itself.
cur.behavior: Settles in one spot and won't shift; strikes back only when struck.

cur.name: Charming beggar
cur.reading: A lineage that gets fed: Charm sharply lowers an opponent's attack by being endearing, Lick can paralyse at close range. Together they suit an animal that lives off what others provide rather than foraging. Fits village and farm edges, where children already play on Snorlax.
cur.behavior: Approaches people and waits to be fed; hard to stay angry at.

cur.name: Larder guard
cur.reading: A lineage that defends its food: Whirlwind blows rivals away from a feeding patch, and Pursuit hits harder at anything that runs off. For an animal that needs 400 kg a day, keeping competitors off is worth the effort. Fits contested feeding grounds such as berry thickets in a lean season.
cur.behavior: Clears a food patch before eating; chases thieves.

cur.name: Torrent striker
cur.reading: A burst-speed lunge and a full-body ram: a lineage built for the fast water the Crystal entry puts it in. Fits plunge pools under falls, where prey is swept past and has to be taken quickly.
cur.behavior: Holds station in the current and strikes out of it.

cur.name: Fog-veiled
cur.reading: Three moves that blunt or screen an opponent's efforts rather than attack. A concealment lineage that fits the Mirage Pokémon's reputation and the weather lore of Dragonair; its place is still, misty water where not being seen is the defence.
cur.behavior: Rarely surfaces; avoids contests rather than winning them.

cur.name: Sonar hunter
cur.reading: A sound attack that confuses and a breath attack to follow it up: a lineage for dark or murky water, such as the cave water of Dragon's Den, where prey must be found without good light.
cur.behavior: Hunts at close range in darkness.

cur.name: Weather-veil
cur.reading: The egg moves closest to the weather lore: a lineage whose 'aura' is mist and screening. Fits still lakes and the den's misty cave water, where concealment matters more than speed.
cur.behavior: Stays hidden in mist; the glow seen through fog is what people report.

cur.name: Sky-leaper
cur.reading: Speed, a full-body ram and a build-up dance: the lineage most likely to produce the occasional wingless flights (148.8). Fits open lakes and coasts, where it is said to live.
cur.behavior: Launches from the water in bursts; seen in the air more than others.

cur.name: Breath-caster
cur.reading: A sound attack to confuse and a breath attack to strike: a hunting lineage for dark or turbid water such as Dragon's Den.
cur.behavior: Hunts close and in the dark.

cur.name: Fog-bank dragon
cur.reading: Dragonair's weather lore in heritable form: Mist shrouds it and blocks stat-lowering, Haze wipes out every stat change on the field, and Light Screen softens special attacks. A defensive lineage that hides in weather rather than making it. Fits fog-bound lakes and sea cliffs where the air is usually thick.
cur.behavior: Stays in mist and low cloud; seldom seen in clear weather.

cur.name: Long-haul flier
cur.reading: A speed lineage: Extreme Speed always strikes first, Dragon Dance builds speed and power together, Dragon Rush is a full-body charge. It is the circle-the-globe canon as an inheritance. Fits open ocean, where distances are huge and storms must be outrun.
cur.behavior: Ranges further than most; arrives fast and leaves fast.

cur.name: Den-pool caller
cur.reading: A lineage built for murky, enclosed water: Supersonic disorients with sound, which carries where light doesn't, and Dragon Breath can paralyse at close range. Fits cave pools like the Dragon's Den, where a confused animal is easy to take.
cur.behavior: Calls in the dark; the young of the cave pools.

cur.name: Rooted meadow
cur.reading: A lineage that settles: Ingrain anchors it and draws health from the ground, and Leech Seed drains whatever stays near it. Together they make a sit-and-drain animal that holds one patch instead of roaming. Fits damp lowland meadow with deep soil.
cur.behavior: Picks a spot, roots, and lets rivals weaken; rarely moves once settled.
cur.analogy: Mistletoes (Viscum) are hemiparasites: they photosynthesise but take water and minerals from a host, which is roughly what Leech Seed on top of Synthesis would look like.

cur.name: Lullaby grazer
cur.reading: The calming-scent canon pushed further: Grass Whistle puts an opponent to sleep with a tune, and Aromatherapy keeps its own group free of status problems. A lineage that ends fights before they start. Fits open grassland crowded with other grazers.
cur.behavior: Answers a threat with song and scent rather than a charge; tolerant of close neighbours.

cur.name: Vine wrestler
cur.reading: A physical lineage: vines to lash and grip, Wring Out to squeeze (strongest against a healthy opponent), Counter to return a blow, and Body Slam for the adult's weight. Fits brushy edges and thickets where predators come close before they are seen.
cur.behavior: Grapples rather than calms; a Meganium that holds its ground.

cur.name: Wildfire charger
cur.reading: The rage canon made into a lineage: Howl raises its attack, Flare Blitz is a burning full-body charge that hurts the user too, and Thrash is an uncontrolled rampage. An animal that answers threats with all-out attack, matching the Typhlosion that ignites anything touching it at the peak of its rage. Fits dry, open grassland where there is nowhere to hide.
cur.behavior: Builds to a howl, then charges in flames; dangerous to everything nearby, including grass.

cur.name: Grass-root forager
cur.reading: A clawed, searching lineage: Foresight finds hidden or evasive targets, and Fury Swipes and Crush Claw rake and tear. A digger and seeker of things hidden in turf and soil rather than a fire-fighter. Fits short grassland and field edges with soft soil.
cur.behavior: Noses through the turf and claws out what it finds; uses fire less.

cur.name: Ember pilferer
cur.reading: A timid opportunist: Covet snatches what the target is holding, Quick Attack gets in and out first, and Extrasensory is an odd psychic sense that would help it judge when to move. The shy Cyndaquil temperament carried into adulthood, taking food rather than fighting for it. Fits farm edges and settlements where food is lying about.
cur.behavior: Steals and runs; flares only when cornered.

cur.name: Mudbank lurker
cur.reading: Mud Sport and Water Sport both coat the body, in mud or water, and Aqua Jet is a strike that lands before the target can act. Together they suggest a lineage that lies coated in silt in shallow, muddy margins and takes prey with a first-strike lunge, the slow-then-sudden habit of the adult pushed further. Fits slow lowland rivers and marsh edges more than clear highland streams.
cur.behavior: Lies half-buried at the edge; the first a prey animal knows of it is the lunge.

cur.name: Boulder-river crusher
cur.reading: Crunch and Metal Claw are hard-contact bites and strikes, and Rock Slide brings stones down. A lineage of rocky, fast-running water that works among boulders and crushes hard-bodied prey, using the line's jaws that can crush anything. Fits steep highland rivers of the kind around Blackthorn.
cur.behavior: Pries and crushes among stones in the current instead of waiting in mud.

cur.name: Thrashing displayer
cur.reading: Dragon Dance raises speed and strength in the games, which reads as a vigorous display that also readies the body to charge; Thrash and Dragon Claw are the sustained, slashing fight that follows. A lineage where rivals settle contests by display and open charge rather than ambush. Fits crowded waters where many adults meet.
cur.behavior: Dances and gapes before it charges; rivals fight in the open.

cur.name: Sound hunter
cur.reading: A lineage that hunts by sound in deeper darkness: an ultrasonic call and an attack out of the dark. Fits dense, dark forest like Ilex, where sight alone fails.
cur.behavior: Calls more and hunts later into the night.

cur.name: Canopy ambusher
cur.reading: A lineage that drops onto prey from a perch without warning. Fits closed-canopy forest with plenty of perches and prey on the branches.
cur.behavior: Waits motionless on one foot, then strikes from above.

cur.name: Display mimic
cur.reading: A lineage given to social display: copying others' actions and showy feather displays. Fits dense owl populations where neighbours have to be told apart and territories advertised.
cur.behavior: Mirrors rivals and fluffs its feathers at them.
cur.analogy: In real birds, ritualised feather displays are mostly for courtship and territory.

cur.name: Dive hunter
cur.reading: A lineage built for fast, powerful strikes from height. Fits open country and forest edges where prey is spotted from tall perches and the approach is long.
cur.behavior: Hunts from high perches over clearings rather than inside the forest.

cur.name: Shadow stalker
cur.reading: A lineage that pushes further into darkness and strikes where the prey can't see it coming. Fits dense, old forest like Ilex.
cur.behavior: Hunts the darkest hours under the thickest canopy.

cur.name: Flusher
cur.reading: A lineage that drives prey out of cover with wind and sound before striking. Fits grassland and reedbeds where prey hides low.
cur.behavior: Beats and calls over cover, then pounces on whatever bolts.

cur.name: Sleeper's bat
cur.reading: A lineage that feeds on hosts it has put to sleep: Hypnosis induces sleep, and Feint Attack is an approach that never misses. A quiet way to take blood from a large animal without a struggle. Fits pasture and farmland near cave roosts, where large animals sleep in the open.
cur.behavior: Lands beside a sleeping animal, keeps it asleep, feeds and leaves before it wakes.
cur.analogy: Common vampire bats mostly feed on sleeping livestock, approaching on the ground.

cur.name: Wind-rider
cur.reading: A lineage for open air: Gust and Whirlwind are blasts of wing-driven air, Brave Bird a reckless full-speed dive. A strong, fast flier that commutes far from its roost to feed. Fits windy highland ridges and sea cliffs.
cur.behavior: Flies further and higher than cave-bound kin; dives on prey in the open.

cur.name: Fleeing-prey hawk
cur.reading: A chaser rather than a sneak: Pursuit hits harder at prey that tries to flee, Quick Attack closes the distance first. A lineage that takes active, flying prey on the wing. Fits forest edges and clearings at night, where flying prey is abundant.
cur.behavior: Hunts moving prey in the air; less dependent on sleeping hosts.

cur.name: Stormfield flock
cur.reading: Charge stores power for the next discharge, while Reflect and Safeguard shield the user and its companions from harm and from status effects. Together they suggest a lineage that holds a large charge and spends it protecting the group rather than attacking. Fits exposed upland pasture where a flock has no cover.
cur.behavior: Bunches tightly when threatened, wool bristling with charge.

cur.name: Dust-kicker
cur.reading: Sand Attack throws grit into an attacker's eyes, and Take Down and Body Slam are full-weight rams. A lineage that defends on the ground, blinding and then barging. Fits dry, dusty steppe where static builds easily and soil is loose.
cur.behavior: Kicks up dust, then charges with its head down.

cur.name: Bleating sentinel
cur.reading: Odor Sleuth is a sniffing-out move and Screech a piercing cry. A lineage that smells danger first and raises the alarm loudly. Fits grassland bordered by scrub or woods, where predators approach from cover.
cur.behavior: Sniffs the wind often and screams at anything it can't see.

cur.name: Foresight line
cur.reading: Detect avoids an attack seen coming, Wish lays down healing that arrives a turn later, and Endure holds on through a blow. With Future Sight, the set describes a lineage that acts ahead of events, stepping out of the way and preparing recovery before it's needed. Fits exposed high meadows where weather and predators arrive fast and cover is scarce.
cur.behavior: Moves out of the way before anything has happened.

cur.name: Hearth companion
cur.reading: Charm softens an attacker, Yawn makes it drowsy, and Tickle lowers its guard. A lineage that defuses trouble rather than fighting it, suited to living closely with people. Fits towns and homesteads, the urban habitat the Gen 3 Pokédex gives every Eevee form.
cur.behavior: Ends a quarrel by making everyone too sleepy, or too charmed, to keep it up.

cur.name: Moonwatch sentinel
cur.reading: Detect reads an attack in time to avoid it, Endure holds on through a blow, and Curse trades speed for toughness. Together they make a patient, hardened ambusher that sits still for long periods and outlasts whatever finds it. Fits rocky ground and ruins with deep shadow to wait in.
cur.behavior: Waits longer than anything else on the hillside; hard to flush and harder to hurt.

cur.name: Lull hunter
cur.reading: Yawn makes a target drowsy, and Tickle and Fake Tears lower its guard. A lineage that disarms prey before the leap instead of relying on darkness alone. Fits the lit edges of towns, where full darkness is rare.
cur.behavior: Settles near its prey, yawning, until the prey settles too.

cur.name: Yard thief
cur.reading: Covet steals what the target holds, and Charm softens an attacker's blows. A lineage that lives off people's stores at night by theft and disarming manners rather than hunting. Fits the towns and farms the Gen 3 Pokédex already files every Eevee form under.
cur.behavior: Raids larders after dark and is forgiven by morning.

cur.name: Barbed bark
cur.reading: A lineage whose defence is chemical and projectile rather than explosive: barbs in the bark case and a toxic litter of shed fragments beneath its tree. Fits dense woods where predators approach from below.
cur.behavior: Explodes less, sheds more; leaves a poisoned ring of debris under its roost.

cur.name: Ground-fall brawler
cur.reading: A lineage that turns the drop from the branch into a fight: retaliation moves (Counter, Revenge) for the animal that shook its tree, and Sand Tomb for burying in sand or leaf litter once down. Fits dry, sandy woodland edges where falling is common and climbing back is slow.
cur.behavior: Falls, digs in and hits back rather than exploding.

cur.name: Mirror shell
cur.reading: A lineage that leans into the armour: a defensive screen, and Power Trick, which swaps attack and defence, as the habit of turning that heavy case into the weapon (rolling and ramming).
cur.behavior: Rolls into attackers with its case; the most Forretress-like juvenile.

cur.name: Still sleeper
cur.reading: Bide waits and returns damage, Curse (for a non-Ghost) trades speed for strength and toughness, and Snore works while asleep. A low-energy lineage built around not moving; fits the deepest, food-poorest reaches of a cave.
cur.behavior: Barely stirs; tough to dislodge when it does.

cur.name: Ambush biter
cur.reading: A bite and a startle: a predatory lineage that strikes from a burrow mouth at whatever passes. Fits soft-floored passages where burrows are easy to dig.
cur.behavior: Waits at the mouth of its maze.

cur.name: Rock-borer
cur.reading: Three moves that work rock: a lineage that tunnels through rubble rather than soil. Fits boulder-choked passages like the Violet City end of Dark Cave, where Dunsparce turn up under smashed rocks.
cur.behavior: Lives in the rubble, not the earth.

cur.name: Tall-grass reaper
cur.reading: A patient ambusher: Razor Wind takes a turn to charge before it cuts, and Night Slash is a high-critical strike from cover. A lineage that waits in grass and lands one decisive blow, the Yellow canon of leaping out of tall grass in heritable form. Fits dense tall-grass meadow.
cur.behavior: Waits motionless in long grass; one strike, rarely two.

cur.name: Last-stand fencer
cur.reading: A lineage that fights through injury: Endure survives a blow that would knock it out, Reversal hits hardest when it is nearly beaten, and Counter returns physical attacks double. It suits Scizor's armour-and-bluff life, where it holds its ground instead of fleeing. Fits contested open ground where it can't hide.
cur.behavior: Never runs; most dangerous when hurt.

cur.name: Wing-singer
cur.reading: Wings used for sound and wind rather than flight: Bug Buzz is a damaging vibration, Silver Wind a gust of wing scales that can boost all its stats. A lineage that turns Scizor's non-flying, fast-flapping wings into a weapon and display. Fits open meadow where sound carries.
cur.behavior: Buzzes loudly when threatened, before any display of the pincers.

cur.name: Heat banker
cur.reading: Three moves for storing something inside and releasing it later: read as banking heat or molten material so it can range away from a hot spot for longer. The lineage most likely to cope with a cold highland.
cur.behavior: Charges up at a hot spot, then ranges out into the cold.

cur.name: Fumarole
cur.reading: Smoke and broad hot air rather than flame: a lineage of steaming vents and hot-spring margins rather than lava. Fits the cooler, wetter end of geothermal ground, the kind of place a Swinub's hot spring would offer.
cur.behavior: Sits in steam; vents heat in waves.

cur.name: Molten
cur.reading: Acid Armor melts the body to toughen it, and Curse (for a non-Ghost) trades speed for strength and toughness. A lineage that stays soft and molten instead of relying on a brittle crust; fits only the hottest ground.
cur.behavior: Barely moves; never crusts over.

cur.name: Deep rooter
cur.reading: A move that splits the ground open and one that throws mud: a digging lineage for deep-frozen ground where food is buried deeper, such as the high meadows above the Ice Path.
cur.behavior: Digs deeper pits and leaves broken ground behind it.

cur.name: Ice-tusk line
cur.reading: Ancient Power is what a Piloswine needs to become Mamoswine, and Icicle Spear matches the adult's ice tusks. A lineage on its way to the ice-age giant; fits the coldest, iciest ground.
cur.behavior: More of them reach Mamoswine; armed with ice early.

cur.name: Charging herd
cur.reading: Three full-body charges, the habit Piloswine is known for (it keeps charging, hackles up). A lineage that meets threats head-on; fits open snowfields with nowhere to hide.
cur.behavior: Charges first and roots afterwards.

cur.name: Nest guard
cur.reading: Three moves that strike first. A lineage that defends nest and food by hitting before it is hit, instead of throwing its food away. Fits crowded cliff ledges where thieves come close.
cur.behavior: Keeps its bundle; drives intruders off fast.

cur.name: Snow roller
cur.reading: Two rolling moves: a lineage that travels downslope by rolling, bundle and all. Fits long, open snowfields above the Ice Path, where rolling is cheaper than flying.
cur.behavior: Comes down the mountain tumbling; walks or flies back up.

cur.name: Far-seer
cur.reading: A foresight move is odd for a bird. A lineage reading ahead could be the one behind the tales of Delibird appearing for lost travellers; Aurora Beam is a light display that would carry in the dark of the Ice Path. The most speculative of the three.
cur.behavior: Turns up where it is needed before it is called.

cur.name: Rockfall ram
cur.reading: Head Smash is a headlong ram that hurts the user too, Focus Energy is a gathering-up before the strike, and Body Slam is the full weight thrown in. Together they suggest a lineage that charges head-first through obstacles instead of rolling: the trail-clearing habit made into a way of life. Fits steep scree and avalanche-prone slopes.
cur.behavior: Lowers its head and drives straight through fallen rock.

cur.name: Herd shield
cur.reading: Counter returns a physical blow twice as hard, and Endeavor drags an attacker down to the user's own condition. With Sturdy, which lets it survive any single hit, the pair describes an animal that takes the first charge and gives it back. A lineage whose senior animals stand at the front of the herd. Fits open river flats where a herd with young can be caught in the open.
cur.behavior: Takes the blow meant for the calves, then answers it.

cur.name: Crevasse walker
cur.reading: Fissure splits the ground, Ice Shard flings ice fast, and Ancient Power lifts rock. A lineage at home in frozen, broken ground, working with ice and stone rather than mud. Fits glaciated high country like the upper slopes of Mt. Silver or the Ice Path beside Blackthorn.
cur.behavior: Breaks ice and frozen ground to open a way, or a wallow.

cur.name: Crèche keeper
cur.reading: Helping Hand boosts an ally, Present hands something over, and Psych Up takes on another's state. Together they suggest a lineage built around care in groups: provisioning and supporting young and herd-mates, the milk's response to any nearby baby carried further. Fits settled herds on rich lowland pasture.
cur.behavior: Nurses and guards whatever young are near, its own or not.

cur.name: Pasture brawler
cur.reading: Hammer Arm and Seismic Toss are grappling, throwing attacks, and Reversal hits harder the more hurt the user is. A lineage that turns and fights rather than rolling away, heaving an attacker off the ground and fighting hardest when wounded. Fits open country with predators and no cover to flee to.
cur.behavior: Stands over its calf and throws whatever comes close.

cur.name: Snowfield sleeper
cur.reading: Curse (for a non-Ghost) slows the user while making it tougher, Endure survives a blow that should fell it, and Sleep Talk acts while asleep. With Thick Fat, the combination suggests a lineage that rides out hard seasons by slowing down and resting a great deal. Fits high, cold pasture with long winters, such as the Blackthorn highlands.
cur.behavior: Slow and heavy in winter, dozing through storms but never quite off guard.

cur.name: Bedrock sleeper
cur.reading: A slow, armoured lineage: Curse (in a non-Ghost) raises attack and defence at the cost of speed, and Iron Defense hardens it further. It is the eat-then-sleep-to-grow canon as a temperament: long rests, slow movement, an animal that is very hard to shift. Fits deep, stable rock where nothing hurries it.
cur.behavior: Moves little, sleeps long, and cannot be pushed out of its spot.

cur.name: Ridge rampager
cur.reading: The rampaging adult as a lineage: Dragon Dance raises attack and speed together, Outrage is a sustained rampage, and Stomp crushes underfoot. A mobile, high-energy version of an already destructive animal. Fits high open ridges where it ranges widely.
cur.behavior: Covers more ground than most and rampages often; the one that redraws maps.

cur.name: Challenger
cur.reading: The fight-seeking canon in move form: Pursuit hits a rival that tries to leave, Assurance hits harder at one already hurt, and Focus Energy sets up a decisive blow. A lineage that doesn't let contests end early. Fits crowded mountain ranges where rivals are many and close.
cur.behavior: Follows rivals that withdraw; finishes fights others would abandon.

cur.name: Mudflat brawler
cur.reading: Mud Bomb blinds with a blob of mud, Stomp tramples, and Counter returns a blow twice as hard. A lineage that fights on the soft ground where its rivals flounder, Marshtomp's 'overwhelms foes struggling in mud' kept into adulthood. Fits wide tidal mudflats and estuaries.
cur.behavior: Draws a foe onto the mud and fights it there.

cur.name: Storm-wall mason
cur.reading: Ancient Power lifts and hurls rock, Double-Edge is a full-weight ram, and Curse trades speed for toughness. A lineage given over to building and holding ground, moving stone and bracing against what comes. Fits exposed rocky coasts where storms hit hardest and the nest needs the strongest wall.
cur.behavior: Builds higher walls than its neighbours and sits behind them.

cur.name: Channel ambusher
cur.reading: Whirlpool traps a target in a vortex, and Bite seizes it. A lineage that hunts in moving water, holding prey in the current and then taking it. Fits tidal channels and river mouths with strong flow.
cur.behavior: Lurks where the current narrows and spins up a trap.

cur.name: Cold-river sleeper
cur.reading: Ice Ball rolls a growing ball of ice, and Yawn brings on drowsiness. Read together, a lineage of cold, slow water that spends long spells buried and torpid, as Mudkip already rests covered in mud on the river bottom. Fits icy highland streams such as those around Blackthorn.
cur.behavior: Winters half-asleep in the mud of a cold river bed.

cur.name: Cloud dancer
cur.reading: Feather Dance buries an attacker in down, blunting its attack, and Agility is a burst of speed. A lineage that turns its dancing flight (334.1) into defence, shedding down and outflying trouble. Fits open mountain skies with strong updrafts.
cur.behavior: Answers a threat with a dazzling, feather-shedding display and then is gone.

cur.name: Mobbing flock
cur.reading: Pursuit strikes a fleeing target, Rage builds with every hit taken, and Dragon Rush is a full-body charge. A lineage whose flocks chase and harry intruders together rather than hiding. Fits forest edges near towns, where Swablu flocks gather in spring and predators follow them.
cur.behavior: The whole flock turns on a hawk and drives it off.
cur.analogy: Many small songbirds mob predators in groups, harassing them until they leave.

cur.name: Fog-bank flock
cur.reading: Haze clears every stat change on the field, and Power Swap trades the user's attacking changes with a foe's. A lineage that neutralises an attacker's advantage rather than fighting it, at home in cloud and mist. Fits cloud-wrapped peaks where visibility is poor and fights are short and confused.
cur.behavior: Disappears into cloud; whatever followed it comes out no stronger than it went in.

cur.name: Deepwater lantern
cur.reading: Confuse Ray is a dazzling light that confuses, Hypnosis lulls to sleep, and Light Screen is a shield of light. With the pink glow of 350.2, the set suggests a lineage that works with light in the dark: dazzling, lulling and shielding at depth. Fits deep, dark lake bottoms.
cur.behavior: Glows in the depths; whatever comes close becomes drowsy and confused.

cur.name: Fog-lake peacemaker
cur.reading: Mist shrouds the user in a protective fog, and Haze wipes out every stat change on the field, read here as damping down a fight for everyone in it. A lineage whose calming is built into its repertoire as well as its looks. Fits cold, often-misty mountain lakes.
cur.behavior: Rises in the fog when the water is disturbed, and the disturbance stops.

cur.name: Weedbed dweller
cur.reading: Mud Sport coats the user in mud, and Tickle lowers a foe's guard by distraction. A lineage that keeps to the muddy, weed-choked shallows of Feebas's youth rather than moving to deep lakes. Fits small, weedy, eutrophic ponds.
cur.behavior: Stays in the weeds and mud where it hatched; rarely seen in open water.

cur.name: Horn-charger
cur.reading: Megahorn is a ramming horn strike, Zen Headbutt a head blow, and Double-Edge a full-weight charge. A lineage that uses its horn as a weapon rather than a sensor, meeting threats head-on. Fits contested ridges where retreat is not possible.
cur.behavior: Lowers its horn and charges instead of slipping away.

cur.name: Decoy shadow
cur.reading: Substitute leaves a decoy, Baton Pass hands off and withdraws, and Feint Attack strikes unseen. A lineage built to avoid being taken: decoys and disappearances in place of fighting. Fits mountains where it is hunted, as the Platinum entry describes.
cur.behavior: Seen once, then gone; trackers follow the wrong trail.

cur.name: Snowfield watcher
cur.reading: Curse trades speed for toughness, and Mean Look pins a target with a stare so it can't flee. A lineage that holds still on open snow and stares down whatever approaches, rather than retreating. Fits high snowfields like Platinum's Mt. Coronet slopes.
cur.behavior: Stands motionless on a snow ridge, watching the valley for days.

cur.name: Four-limb striker
cur.reading: The canon fighting style made heritable: burning fists, a burning kick, and a two-footed kick. A lineage that commits to close striking with hands and feet rather than flame at range. Fits narrow ledges where there's no room to keep distance.
cur.behavior: Closes in fast and strikes with every limb; uses its fire as a glove, not a torch.

cur.name: Troop helper
cur.reading: A cooperative lineage: Helping Hand strengthens a packmate's attack, Assist borrows a packmate's move, and Fake Out makes an attacker flinch so the group can act first. Fits the ranked packs Monferno lives in, on crags where a troop defends one stretch of cliff together.
cur.behavior: Fights alongside others and covers them; low-ranked animals that make themselves useful.

cur.name: Cliff trickster
cur.reading: A lineage that wins by reading its opponent: Encore locks an attacker into repeating its last move, Counter returns physical blows, and Focus Energy readies a decisive hit. Together they make fights short and predictable. Fits crowded cliff colonies where conflicts are frequent and must not be costly.
cur.behavior: Baits, waits and punishes; rarely the first to commit.

cur.name: Long-dive hunter
cur.reading: A lineage built for longer and faster dives: Aqua Ring wraps it in a veil of water that heals it a little each turn, Agility sharpens its speed, and Hydro Pump is a heavy strike at range. Together they extend the ten-minute dives of the canon. Fits deep, cold open water where prey is far down and scattered.
cur.behavior: Dives longer and further offshore than others; rarely seen on land.

cur.name: Shore peacemaker
cur.reading: The adult's restraint made heritable: Feather Dance is a display that sharply lowers an opponent's attack, Yawn makes it drowsy, Supersonic confuses it. Ways to end a dispute without blood. Fits crowded shore colonies where proud animals must live close together.
cur.behavior: Displays and lulls before it ever strikes; more tolerant of neighbours.

cur.name: Tideflat prober
cur.reading: A lineage of mud rather than ice: Mud-Slap and Mud Sport both use mud (one to blind, one to blunt electric attacks), and Double Hit strikes twice in quick succession, like rapid probing. Fits muddy estuaries and tidal flats, a warmer, shallower shore than the canon's icy seas.
cur.behavior: Forages in the shallows at low tide; dives less.

cur.name: Thorn thicket
cur.reading: Roselia's thorn-shooting made heritable and extended: Pin Missile fires a volley of thorns, Spikes scatters barbs on the ground. A lineage that defends a fixed patch, like a dense flowerbed, from browsers and flower thieves rather than hunting. Fits crowded meadow and garden edges where its blooms draw trouble.
cur.behavior: Holds a patch, fires at anything that reaches for a flower, and litters the approach with barbs.

cur.name: Sleeping lure
cur.reading: The scent lure with a sedative behind it: Sleep Powder puts the animal it has drawn in to sleep, Cotton Spore slows anything that tries to leave, and Mind Reader makes the next strike certain. A sit-and-wait trap that needs no venom to work. Fits sheltered pond margins where prey come to drink.
cur.behavior: Lures, drugs and only then strikes; rarely needs to chase.

cur.name: Sun-fed bloom
cur.reading: A lineage that leans on sunlight rather than prey: Synthesis for recovery in the sun, Razor Leaf for everyday defence, Leaf Storm as a single all-out burst that costs it afterwards. Fits open, sunny grassland where prey is scarce and light is not.
cur.behavior: Basks more and lures less; hits hard once when threatened, then retreats to recover.

cur.name: Sand-trap lurker
cur.reading: Three moves that all stop prey getting away: Sand Tomb traps it in sand, Mud Shot and Scary Face slow it. Gible's pounce-from-the-nest canon turned into a whole strategy. Fits sandy or silty cave floors where prey passes the nest mouth.
cur.behavior: Stays at its nest hole longer than most Gible; holds what it catches rather than chasing.

cur.name: Wind-cutter
cur.reading: A lineage that attacks at range from the air: Twister whips up wind and Dragon Breath can paralyse. It is the move version of the Platinum folklore that its wings cut blades of wind. Fits open high country where prey is spotted and hit from a distance.
cur.behavior: Strikes from the air without closing in; leaves flattened brush where it hunts.
cur.note: Built partly on a folklore entry (445.3).

cur.name: Clumsy rampager
cur.reading: Gible's clumsiness made into a temperament: Thrash and Outrage are multi-turn rampages that leave it confused, and Double-Edge hurts the user. A lineage that wins by overwhelming force and pays for it. Fits crowded nesting caves where fights between neighbours are short and violent.
cur.behavior: Fights in frenzies; often injured, rarely beaten.

cur.name: Canyon runner
cur.reading: Riolu's three-mountains-in-a-night canon made into a lineage: Agility for speed, High Jump Kick for clearing gaps and ledges, Low Kick for taking down heavy animals at the legs. Fits broken canyon country where ground is crossed at a run and in leaps.
cur.behavior: Covers enormous ground every night; strikes from a jump.

cur.name: Reading jaw
cur.reading: A lineage that hunts with its jaws: Mind Reader makes the next move certain to land, and Bite and Crunch put the jaws, otherwise absent from the line's own list, behind it. Aura reading plus a sure bite is the shape of an ambush hunter. Fits forest edge where prey moves under cover.
cur.behavior: Waits until it has read the animal's next movement, then bites once.

cur.name: Pack shield
cur.reading: A guardian lineage: Follow Me draws attacks onto itself, Detect dodges them, and Iron Defense hardens it to take what gets through. It pairs with Riolu's aura alarm: one animal hears the fear and stands in front. Fits open mountainside where a group with young must cross exposed ground.
cur.behavior: Moves toward a frightened groupmate and takes the threat on itself.

cur.name: Nest-raiding pair
cur.reading: The Platinum pair tactic carried in the blood: Fake Out makes a guarding parent flinch, Spite wears down its defences, and Assist lets either partner use the other's moves, so the decoy and the thief can swap roles. Fits snowline forest where tree-nesting birds breed.
cur.behavior: Works in twos; one draws the parents off while the other takes the eggs.

cur.name: Rime sprinter
cur.reading: A first-strike lineage: Ice Shard always goes first, Crush Claw tears and weakens the target's defence, and Double Hit strikes twice. A hunt decided in one rush. Fits open snowfields and ice where prey sees you coming and only speed works.
cur.behavior: Short, explosive chases across open snow; gives up fast if the first rush fails.

cur.name: Cave-mouth tracker
cur.reading: A lineage that hunts what hides or runs: Foresight finds evasive or hidden targets, Pursuit hits harder at prey that tries to flee, and Bite holds what it catches. Fits broken rock and cave entrances like Mt. Silver's, where prey either hides in cracks or bolts.
cur.behavior: Checks every crevice; never lets a fleeing animal go.

cur.name: Glacier relict
cur.reading: The most Mamoswine-like Swinub: Icicle Spear fires icicles in a volley, the tusks-of-ice canon in move form, and Ancient Power is the very move a Piloswine needs to evolve. A lineage that carries its own evolution trigger from the egg. Fits permanent ice, the habitat its ancestors thrived in.
cur.behavior: Grows into a Mamoswine without help; keeps to the coldest ground.

cur.name: Moraine rammer
cur.reading: Piloswine's charging made heavier: Double-Edge and Body Slam are full-weight hits, and Rock Slide brings down stones. A lineage of rocky glacial debris where a charge sends rock tumbling. Fits moraine slopes and scree below ice fields.
cur.behavior: Charges harder and more often; loose rock comes down behind it.

cur.name: Frost-ground breaker
cur.reading: A digger for the hardest ground: Fissure splits the earth, Mud Shot throws wet soil, and Curse makes it slower but stronger and tougher. A lineage that breaks frozen soil to reach buried food, building on Swinub's frozen-ground nose. Fits permafrost tundra where food lies under a hard crust.
cur.behavior: Slow, methodical, leaves cracked and turned ground behind it.
